architecture.correctionSeparationLaw: Model-correctable Runtime/Tool rejection and caller/domain conclusion rejection are different execution mechanics. Tool rejection consumes maxToolCorrections/toolCorrections; conclusion rejection consumes maxConclusionCorrections/conclusionCorrections.
architecture.ownerAdmissionLaw: Harness hosts the correction boundary but does not own domain truth. A caller/domain validate_conclusion rejection remains owner-authored semantic admission and Harness forwards that exact reason without assuming incompleteness or missing evidence.
architecture.compatibilityLaw: Schema-v1 Run Contracts may omit the later maxConclusionCorrections field and materialize historical default 3. An explicitly bound maxToolCorrections value does not implicitly bind conclusion correction. Unknown budget fields still fail closed.
architecture.effectLaw: Conclusion correction does not grant Tool or external-effect authority. The Finance acceptance used zero Tool calls, no dispatch claim, and no external financial write.
architecture.nonPromotionLaw: This change does not add a generic semantic verifier, domain ontology, truth service, or optimizer. It only separates correction mechanics already present in the Agent loop.

observedFailures: Finance authority/notional rejection was described by Harness as incomplete/missing evidence even though evidence was not missing.
Conclusion rejection incremented toolCorrections and was blocked by maxToolCorrections despite toolCalls=0.

One natural Finance Run corrected delegated size 13 -> 13 -> 12 and succeeded, while another exhausted the shared correction budget, proving both value and friction of the existing owner-admission hook.

implementation.feedback: Harness conclusion gate rejected this candidate conclusion. Correct the candidate using the caller/domain rejection reason below; use available tools or evidence only when relevant: <owner reason>

conclusion: Real Finance owner-admission pressure justifies separating conclusion correction from Tool correction, not adding a new semantic authority layer. Harness now carries an independent conclusion-correction budget/counter and reason-neutral owner feedback. A zero Tool-correction budget no longer disables a legitimate caller/domain conclusion repair; the tested Finance 65 USD candidate was rejected and corrected to the admitted 60 USD candidate with toolCorrections=0 and conclusionCorrections=1.
knownLimits: maxConclusionCorrections defaults to 3 for backward-compatible schema-v1 materialization; this is a bounded execution default, not a claim that three attempts are universally optimal.
A caller/domain validate_conclusion implementation must still have legitimate owner semantics. Harness independence does not create truth authority.
Conclusion admission is not Task optimization. A domain may admit a lawful candidate that is not the best candidate for the Task.

The Finance dogfood observed one non-decodable terminal conclusion under structured-result-v1, but exact terminal provenance was not captured. This implementation deliberately does not change structured fallback behavior; deterministic reproduction remains required.

The 273-test full suite ran on the portable implementation tree before the unrelated global-secondary evidence-only commit. Git tree comparison proves src+tests identity with the final implementation revision, and exact final targeted/Finance checks were rerun after cherry-pick.
